name: Taking Back Sunday
label: Victory
lede: A Long Island band made a $10,000 record that went platinum, lost half its members to a fight over a sister and a song credit, sold more than any Victory band ever, and then, a decade later, got the old line-up back in a room.

eras.title: Amityville, and the first fight
eras.text: Taking Back Sunday began in Amityville, Long Island, with a bassist who'd soon leave to start Brand New, and the first falling-out became one of emo's great rivalries. A kid from North Carolina drifted in on bass and ended up the singer.

years.h: Eddie Reyes and Jesse Lacey start Taking Back Sunday
years.p: With John Nolan on lead guitar, Antonio Longo singing and Steven DeJoseph drumming. The name comes from a song by Long Island band The Waiting Process.

years.h: Jesse Lacey quits after a clash with John Nolan, starts [[Brand New|9311e2bc-bb3f-44cf-90d8-b1fe6912b60b]]
years.p: Lacey left after what Wikipedia calls a personal incident with Nolan, formed Brand New, and the feud spilled onto records, including Brand New's Seventy Times 7.
years.xp:
It became, in Wikipedia's words, one of the most public intra-band rivalries in emo history. Seventy Times 7 appeared on Brand New's 2001 debut Your Favorite Weapon.

Nolan and Lacey eventually reconciled, though Adam Lazzara was still speaking about Lacey unfavorably in 2015.

years.h: Adam Lazzara switches from bass to lead vocals
years.p: Lazzara had moved up from North Carolina after meeting the band at a show and joined on bass. Mark O'Connell replaces drummer Steven DeJoseph and Shaun Cooper takes the bass.

years.h: Taking Back Sunday signs to Victory Records off a demo
years.p: A friend passed their demo to Victory A&R rep Angel Juarbe. The band was in the studio the same month.

eras.title: Tell All Your Friends
eras.text: Two weeks, $10,000 and a Jersey City studio produced a debut that sold 2,000 copies its first week and then never stopped. By the time it broke, the band that made it was falling apart on stage.

years.cap: Tell All Your Friends, Victory Records, 2002
years.h: Tell All Your Friends: a $10,000 record goes platinum
years.p: Made in two weeks at Big Blue Meenie in Jersey City with Sal Villanueva. It sold 2,000 copies in week one, went gold in 2005 and platinum in June 2023.
years.xp:
It became Victory's bestseller, spending 68 weeks on Billboard's Heatseekers chart and 78 on Independent Albums. Alternative Press called it one of the scene's most celebrated and influential releases.

The Cute Without the 'E' (Cut from the Team) video riffs on Fight Club; the You're So Last Summer video features Flavor Flav.
play: Cute Without the 'E' (Cut from the Team)

years.h: First video: Great Romances of the 20th Century
years.p: Directed by Christian Winters, released three weeks before the album and sent to radio March 12.

years.src: Wikipedia: Taking Back Sunday · Wikipedia: Straylight Run
years.h: John Nolan and Shaun Cooper quit Taking Back Sunday
years.p: Per Wikipedia, Adam Lazzara was drinking heavily and had cheated on Nolan's sister Michelle. Nolan found his Skate & Surf apology insincere; two days later he and Cooper were gone.
years.xp:
The official reason was exhaustion from touring. Wikipedia says the truth also involved constant fighting and disputes over songwriting credit.

Nolan and Cooper formed [[Straylight Run|ffe16bba-4d84-409b-8f22-5242c60b930f]] with Michelle DaRosa (Nolan's sister) and Will Noon. Their 2004 debut, also on Victory, sold over 11,000 copies in its first week.

years.h: Fred Mascherino and Matt Rubano join Taking Back Sunday
years.p: Two jazz-trained players: Mascherino from [[Breaking Pangaea|b2f5dbf0-572f-419e-a3c0-7d0cae9c609c]] on guitar and vocals, Rubano on bass. Lazzara said they cleaned up and tightened the band's sound.

eras.title: Victory's biggest week, then Warner
eras.text: The second Victory album debuted at No. 3, still the label's highest chart peak, and Tony Brummel fought the RIAA over its gold record. Then Taking Back Sunday went to a major and did even better.

years.src: Wikipedia: Where You Want to Be
years.h: Where You Want to Be debuts at No. 3 with 163,000
years.p: Self-financed and produced by Lou Giordano in Brooklyn and Hoboken. It sold 634,000 by June 2005, still Victory's highest chart peak, and the best-selling independent rock album within a year of release.
years.xp: It topped Billboard's Independent Albums chart for 50 weeks, and Rolling Stone named it one of the top fifty records of 2004. The This Photograph Is Proof (I Know You Know) video was directed by [[Blink-182|0743b15a-3c32-48c8-ad58-cb325350befa]]'s Tom DeLonge, shot across Dallas, Los Angeles and Nashville in 48 hours.

q: another attempt by the RIAA and its major-label partners to victimize
years.src: Wikipedia: Where You Want to Be
years.h: Victory's first gold record, and Tony Brummel attacks the RIAA
years.p: Where You Want to Be is certified gold, a first for a Victory artist. Victory founder Tony Brummel objected to the certification; the band's manager Jillian Newman pushed back.
years.xp: Brummel framed the certification as the major-label industry trying to belittle an independent. Manager Jillian Newman countered his objection publicly.

years.h: Taking Back Sunday signs to Warner Bros.
years.p: The band leaves Victory after two albums; Victory keeps releasing compilations from the catalog.

years.h: Louder Now hits No. 2
years.p: Recorded at Barefoot Studios in Los Angeles with Eric Valentine, producer of [[Queens of the Stone Age|7dc8f5bd-9d0b-4087-9f73-dc164950bbd8]]' Songs for the Deaf. It sold over 900,000 copies.

years.h: Victory cashes in with Notes from the Past
years.p: A Victory compilation of four Tell All Your Friends songs, six from Where You Want to Be and two B-sides.

q: There were just problems between the five of us about writing.
years.h: Fred Mascherino leaves for The Color Fred
years.p: Mascherino said the five of them had problems over who would write and how. Matthew Fazzi replaces him.
years.xp: Mascherino went on to focus on his solo project The Color Fred. Guitarist and backing vocalist Matthew Fazzi took his place for New Again.

eras.title: The originals come home
eras.text: After one album with Matthew Fazzi, the band admitted it wasn't having fun. John Nolan and Shaun Cooper, whose Straylight Run had just gone on hiatus, came back, and the Tell All Your Friends line-up was whole again.

years.h: New Again, the Matthew Fazzi album
years.p: Taking Back Sunday's fourth record, previewed by Sink into Me on Zane Lowe's BBC Radio 1 show in April.

years.src: Wikipedia: Taking Back Sunday · Wikipedia: Straylight Run
years.h: John Nolan and Shaun Cooper rejoin Taking Back Sunday
years.p: Matt Rubano and Matthew Fazzi left March 29. The band said it had been miserable and felt it wasn't Taking Back Sunday without the originals; meeting in Texas, the chemistry was still there.

years.h: The self-titled album, with Eric Valentine again
years.p: The reunited five's first record, led by Faith (When I Let You Down) in May.

eras.title: Anniversaries and a coin toss
eras.text: Taking Back Sunday started playing its own history back: the debut in full, then a twentieth-anniversary tour where a coin decided the setlist. Along the way a founder left to deal with alcoholism.

years.h: Tell All Your Friends played in full for its 10th
years.p: With [[Bayside|5f821136-9935-403c-abb5-e78ddda35e9f]] as main support. The same summer, Taking Back Sunday plays every date of the 2012 Warped Tour.

years.h: Underoath's Spencer Chamberlain sings for Adam Lazzara
years.p: Lazzara's son was born prematurely, and [[Underoath|674a7e8c-9682-419a-8e05-2358e28b5359]]'s Spencer Chamberlain filled in for nine shows.

years.h: Happiness Is on Hopeless Records
years.p: The sixth album, with violinist Dylan Ebrahimian, who played with the band at an acoustic show at Stony Brook University in November 2013.

years.h: Tidal Wave
years.p: Taking Back Sunday's seventh album, written between tours for Happiness Is.

years.h: Founder Eddie Reyes leaves, citing his battle with alcoholism
years.p: The last founding member besides John Nolan steps away, saying he hoped to come back one day.

years.cap: The coin that picked the setlist
years.h: Twentieth-anniversary tour: a coin picks the album
years.p: On two-night stands, a specially made coin decided whether night one got Louder Now or Where You Want to Be. Tell All Your Friends got played every night. The Twenty compilation came out the same day.

eras.title: 152, and a drummer's lawsuit
eras.text: Free of labels for a while, Taking Back Sunday made a record on Fantasy and played Coachella. Then its drummer of 23 years walked, and went to court.

years.h: Verrazzano Villains with Wu-Tang's Cappadonna
years.p: A collaboration with Q-Unique, DJ Eclipse and [[Wu-Tang Clan|0febdcf7-4e1f-4661-9493-b40427de2c13]]'s Cappadonna. In June, Taking Back Sunday plays shows with [[Thursday|0acae232-d31a-4211-b6d0-6af1b6350274]] and [[Piebald|403bc4cd-602c-4b59-8379-05cb24f66aa6]].

years.h: 152 on Fantasy Records
years.p: Taking Back Sunday's eighth album and first original new music in over four years. They play Coachella in April 2024.

years.h: Fred Mascherino plays with Taking Back Sunday again
years.p: At Starland Ballroom in Sayreville, New Jersey, his first time on stage with the band since 2007, for Liar (It Takes One to Know One) and MakeDamnSure.

years.h: Mark O'Connell announces he's out after 23 years
years.p: Eddie Reyes had already said so on a podcast in December. O'Connell cited creative differences and a lack of support while he committed to sobriety.

years.h: Mark O'Connell sues his former bandmates
years.p: A defamation suit alleging false claims and withheld royalty payments.

years.h: Fred Mascherino back on tour while John Nolan takes a break
years.p: John Nolan steps off the road to spend time with family, and Mascherino rejoins in a touring role. The plan: festival dates as a six-piece with Lazzara, Nolan and Mascherino sharing vocals.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Where You Want to Be
